audience.notes: Australian couples in their 30s, luxury, AUD 150K+ wedding budgets, usually flying long haul straight after the wedding. They want a honeymoon that feels unhurried and considered, and fear planning from the other side of the world with nobody to call, and spending a lot on something generic or overpacked. The paying parent (often gifting part of the honeymoon) wants to see that someone responsible has thought about transfers, timing and what happens if a flight slips. Do not write for the bargain hunter: no deal hacks, no points tricks, no price ranges.

payload.search_intent: Informational with a template need: a reusable day by day structure and a worked sample they can copy, then adapt to a destination.
payload.angle: The structure behind a good honeymoon, not a list of hotels. A printable day by day template, then a two week sample that shows why each day sits where it does: arrive and rest, two bases joined by one deliberate travel day, a slow finish before the long flight home. Every day carries the work most couples never see (transfers, buffers, wet weather plans, documents). It is also the hub every destination honeymoon itinerary on the site links up to.
serp_gaps_to_win: No AU result serves Australian couples flying out; Sydney is inbound-tourism content and a Tripadvisor thread in four slots.
Template intent goes to Pinterest, Etsy and template farms; no expert travel brand owns a printable honeymoon itinerary template.
No ranking page explains the structure of a honeymoon (rest first, two bases, deliberate travel day, slow finish) or the invisible logistics behind each day.
Length queries ('2 week honeymoon', '7 days', '10 days') appear in PAA and related searches without a structured answer.

outline.h2: A two week sample honeymoon itinerary built on structure
outline.answers: What does a well paced 14 day honeymoon look like?
must_include: Days 1 to 3 arrival and rest after the long-haul flight and the wedding; no early starts
Days 4 to 7 first base with one planned thing a day
Day 8 a single deliberate travel day between bases, nothing else booked
Days 9 to 12 second base, different in feel (city to coast, or coast to country)
Days 13 and 14 a slow finish near the departure airport
Placeholders only, no named hotels, airlines, flight times, prices or perks
Why the structure works for couples coming off months of wedding planning

outline.h2: Travel days, transfers and the work you do not see
outline.answers: What has to be arranged behind each day so nothing goes wrong?
must_include: Invisible work section: airport and inter-base transfers booked with names and pick-up points, buffers around connections, a wet weather or rest alternative for each planned day, late check-out and luggage on the last day, who to call if a flight changes
How a Wedded Advisor holds the whole itinerary as one plan (no invented perks; Wedded Privileges only as 'eligible stays may include' wording from /travel)
Answers couple fear 2 (planning from far away, nobody on the ground)
Link /wonderland-concierge and /honeymoon-ideas/honeymoon-planning-service

outline.h2: Documents and timing before you fly
outline.answers: What do we need to check, and when, before an overseas honeymoon?
must_include: Smartraveller linked inline at the claim (https://www.smartraveller.gov.au): check destination advice, subscribe to updates
Passport validity rules vary by destination; check the destination's entry requirements via Smartraveller rather than stating a fixed rule
Name on tickets matching the passport if a name change is planned after the wedding (source required from researcher; official Australian Passport Office page only)
Travel insurance bought when the trip is booked; link the honeymoon insurance article only if live, else [[LINK NEEDED: honeymoon travel insurance]]
A simple countdown (when to book, when to confirm transfers, when to print the itinerary) without invented lead times; researcher to source or keep qualitative

Ten days: two bases, still one travel day
Three weeks: three bases only if each gets four nights or more (editorial guidance, framed as our approach, not a fact)
Minimoon now and full trip later; link /honeymoon-ideas/minimoon or /expert-advice/delayed-honeymoon
